chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, in a mursal report, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

He عليه السلام said: Know—may Allah teach you goodness—that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Eternal, and eternality is His attribute by which the rational person is led to know that there was nothing before Him and nothing with Him in His everlastingness. Thus it has become clear to us, by the acknowledgement of the people generally, through the conclusive force of this attribute, that there was nothing before Allah and nothing with Allah in His abiding, and the statement of one who claims that something was before Him or with Him is invalid. That is because if something had been with Him in His abiding, it would not be permissible for Him to be its Creator, since it would always have been with Him; so how could He be Creator of one that never ceased to be with Him? And if something had been before Him, that thing—not He—would have been first, and the first would have had more right to be the creator of the first.

Then He, Blessed and Exalted, described Himself with names by which, when He created the creatures, obligated them in worship, and tested them, He called them to invoke Him. So He named Himself Hearing, Seeing, Powerful, Standing, Speaking, Manifest, Hidden, Subtle, All-Aware, Strong, Mighty, Wise, Knowing, and whatever resembles these names.

So when the lying deniers saw those among His names, and had heard us relate concerning Allah that nothing is like Him and nothing among creation shares His state, they said: Tell us, if you claim that there is no likeness to Allah and no resemblance to Him, then how do you share with Him in His Most Beautiful Names and call yourselves by all of them? Indeed, in that there is proof that you are like Him in all His states, or in some of them rather than others, since you have gathered the goodly names.

It is said to them: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has assigned to the servants names from His names while the meanings differ. This is like a single name gathering two different meanings. The proof of that is the accepted and widespread speech of people, and it is with that that Allah addressed creation: He spoke to them in what they understand so that it might be a proof against them regarding what they neglected.

A man may be called a dog, a donkey, a bull, sweetness, bitterness, or a lion—all of that despite his being different from those things and their conditions. The names do not apply according to the original meanings upon which they were formed, for a human being is neither a lion nor a dog. So understand that—may Allah have mercy on you.

Allah the Exalted is called Knowing not by a newly occurring knowledge through which He came to know things, using it to preserve what will come of His command, to deliberate over what He creates of His creatures, or to undo what has passed away of what He annihilated of His creation—such that, if that knowledge were absent from Him, He would be ignorant and weak, as is the case with the learned among creation. They are only called knowing because of an acquired knowledge, after having been ignorant, and sometimes knowledge departs from them concerning things and they return to ignorance. Allah is only called Knowing because He is ignorant of nothing. Thus the Creator and the creature share the name 'knowing,' while the meaning differs, as you have seen.

Our Lord is called Hearing, not by means of an aperture in Him by which He hears sound, nor does He see by it, just as our aperture by which we hear does not enable us to see. Rather, He has informed that no sound is hidden from Him. It is not according to the limit by which we are named. So we share the name related to hearing, while the meaning differs.

Likewise with sight: He does not see by an aperture from Himself as we see by an aperture from ourselves, by which we do not benefit for anything else. Rather, Allah is Seeing, not by bearing a visible form looked toward. We share the name, but the meaning differs.

He is Standing, not in the sense of erectness and standing upon a leg under strain as created things stand. Rather, 'standing' here indicates that He is Preserver, as when one says, 'So-and-so is in charge of our affair.' And Allah is the one standing over every soul for what it has earned. 'Standing' also in human speech means remaining, and it also conveys sufficiency, as when you say to a man, 'Take care of the affair of the clan of so-and-so,' meaning suffice them. The one standing among us stands on a leg. Thus we share the name, but not the meaning.

As for the Subtle, it is not in the sense of smallness, fineness, or littleness. Rather, it is in the sense of penetrating through things and being inaccessible to comprehension, as when you say, 'This matter became subtle to me,' or 'So-and-so was subtle in his view and speech,' meaning that the intellect became too constrained to grasp it, pursuit failed, and it became so profound and subtle that imagination cannot reach it. Thus Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is subtle beyond being comprehended by a limit or delimited by a description. Subtlety in us means smallness and littleness. So we share the name while the meaning differs.

As for the All-Aware, He is the one from whom nothing is absent and nothing escapes. This is not through experimentation or taking lessons from things, for in experimentation and reflection there are two forms of knowledge, and without them it would not be known, because one who is like that would be ignorant. Allah has never ceased to be fully aware of what He creates. The 'aware' among people is one who seeks information out of ignorance and learns. Thus we share the name while the meaning differs.

As for the Manifest, it is not because He is above things by mounting over them, sitting upon them, or ascending their heights. Rather, it is because of His subduing things, His prevailing over them, and His power over them—like when a man says, 'I prevailed over my enemies,' or 'Allah gave me victory over my opponent,' indicating triumph and dominance. Such is Allah's manifestation over things.

Another aspect is that He is Manifest to whoever seeks Him, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the disposer of everything He originated. What manifest thing is more apparent and clearer than Allah, Blessed and Exalted? For you do not fail to encounter His workmanship wherever you turn, and within yourself there are enough of His signs. The manifest among us is one outward in himself and known by his limit. The name joins us, but the meaning does not.

As for the Hidden, it is not in the sense of entering into things by delving within them. Rather, from Him it means His inward encompassment of things in knowledge, preservation, and governance—like one who says, 'I came to know his inwardness,' meaning, I became informed about him and knew the hidden secret of him. The hidden among us is one absent within a thing, concealed. We share the name, while the meaning differs.

As for the Subduer, it is not in the sense of exertion, fatigue, contrivance, maneuvering, or deceit, as servants subdue one another, where the subdued may in turn become the subduer and the subduer become subdued. Rather, from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, it means that everything He created is clothed in humbleness before its Maker and has little power to resist what He intends for it. It does not withhold itself from Him even for the blink of an eye when He says to it, 'Be,' and it is. The subduer among us is as I have mentioned and described. Thus we share the name, while the meaning differs.

And so it is with all the names. Even if we have not gathered all of them, reflection upon what we have conveyed to you is sufficient. And Allah is your help and our help in our guidance and our success.

key_terms.اللَّطِيفُ: Subtle; meaning beyond being grasped or delimited.
key_terms.الْأَسْمَاءِ: The divine names by which Allah is described and invoked.
key_terms.الْقَاهِرُ: Subduer; the One before whom all creation is overpowered.
key_terms.الْقِدَمُ: Eternality as a divine attribute indicating absolute pre-existence.
key_terms.بَصِيرٌ: Seeing; for Allah, without created instruments or direction.
key_terms.سَمِيعًا: Hearing; for Allah, not by bodily means or organs.
key_terms.عَالِمًا: Knowing; for Allah, this means never being ignorant of anything.

ai.seo_question: How do the divine names of Allah differ in meaning from the same names used for human beings?
ai.summary: This narration explains that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is eternal and unmatched, with nothing before Him or alongside Him. It clarifies that divine names such as Knowing, Hearing, Seeing, Manifest, Hidden, and Subduer may also be used for creatures, but only as shared words while the realities and meanings differ completely. The hadith is a foundational theological text on tawhid and the proper understanding of the divine attributes in contrast to created qualities.
